advanced_families.title: Text tokenization, sparse document features and topic-model workflows
advanced_families.how_it_works: Tokenized documents preserve text-derived units and metadata; sparse document-term models count vocabulary occurrences. Topic models infer probabilistic document mixtures and word distributions, while preprocessing, language and solver choices affect interpretation.
implementation_steps: Freeze a selected text profile for Unicode normalization, token boundaries, case, punctuation, language, stopwords and empty documents. Retain original document IDs and offsets so every displayed token or removed term can be traced back to the source text.

Implement bounded token streams and sparse document-term storage in Rust, exposing versioned Octave-facing document/model objects. Specify vocabulary order, duplicate/n-gram counting, training-only vocabulary construction and unknown-term behavior; no hidden dense conversion is permitted for large corpora.

Add one declared LDA inference profile with explicit solver, word/topic priors, convergence, RNG and topic-order policy. Evaluate Gensim as an optional candidate, translating prior parameterization and dtype precisely; similar topic labels or default settings do not establish MATLAB object/solver compatibility.

Implement source-generating preprocessing and model inspection with saved data splits and reversible pipeline metadata. Validate held-out transforms without fitting vocabulary or preprocessing on held-out documents. Supervised text models, embeddings, multilingual tokenizers and transformer/GPU backends expand through separately gated operator/data profiles.

Publish original document-count and one-topic workshops with exact numerical fixtures, then add corpus-scale resource and installed rerun checks. Bundle original/licensed teaching text; protect provenance and report unsupported languages or extraction formats instead of silently substituting a different tokenizer.

advanced_families.title: Satellite orbits, ground-station access and reproducible link budgets
advanced_families.how_it_works: Satellite scenarios propagate objects, transform coordinate frames and evaluate visibility over time. Access depends on obstruction and elevation rules; communication links additionally combine propagation loss, antenna gains, receiver noise and rate requirements.
implementation_steps: Define selected scenario records for epochs/time scales, orbital elements or Cartesian states, frame identities, central-body shape/gravity and ground stations. Begin with an explicitly named spherical-Earth, two-body profile; TLE/SGP4, perturbations, terrain and non-Earth bodies remain separate validated variants.

Implement analytical circular/Kepler propagation and declared inertial/Earth-fixed transforms in Rust with original Octave-facing objects. Evaluate NASA SPICE for later frame/time services; pin kernels and conventions before use. Do not mix inertial state, Earth-fixed station coordinates or UTC samples implicitly.

Compute line-of-sight occultation, local elevation masks and access intervals using declared sample grids or refined boundary roots. Specify interval closure and endpoint policy, retain object IDs, and distinguish geometric visibility from radio-link closure or a successfully rendered ground track.

Add selected far-field free-space link budgets with explicit dBW/dBm, dBi, hertz, bits/second, noise temperature and losses. Expose every term and receiver threshold; waveform, coding, atmospheric fading, antenna electromagnetic design and standard compliance require separate domain profiles.

Publish original overhead/occulted geometry, circular-orbit and loss-budget workshops with independent formulas. Export scenario inputs, time/frame profile and reports. Optional platform dynamics, terrain layers, numerical propagation and standards-based radios must close their own AF and external conformance gates before advertising those variants.
advanced_families.ui_design: A Satellite workspace combines an object tree, globe/orbit view and access timeline. Inspectors show epoch, frame, units, propagator and central-body assumptions. Selecting a station/satellite pair reveals range, elevation and obstruction separately from link status. A link-budget table shows gains, losses, noise and bit rate with numeric margins. Timeline sampling and refined interval boundaries are labeled; unsupported TLE, terrain or radio models remain visible prerequisites.
